samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copy re-assigns Yorkie `Long` values as plain JS numbers, re-introducing the 32-bit truncation bug the spreadsheet comment store explicitly works around
samples.evidence: `yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14` documents that Yorkie 0.7.x classifies integer-valued JS numbers as `PrimitiveType.Integer` (32-bit), so comment timestamps must be written as `BigInt` (`toYorkieMs`) to survive the wire; readers coerce back at `yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:16` and `sheet-view.tsx:246-248`. The new `DocumentCopyService.copyContent` sheet/slides/board arm does `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` and then `root[key] = value` (packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts, JSON_ROOT_TYPES branch), which writes every Long back as a plain number. A copied spreadsheet's `sheets[tab].comments[*].createdAt/editedAt` therefore land as truncated Integers and render as 1970 dates for every peer. The identical technique in `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:316` has the same gap, so there is no precedent handling it.

samples.summary: Comment threads ARE carried over for `sheet` (and any type in JSON_ROOT_TYPES) even though the service doc and design doc state comments are deliberately not copied
samples.evidence: Sheet comment threads live inside the Yorkie root (`createWorksheet()` seeds `comments: {}` at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:147, and `sheet-view.tsx:252` reads `root.sheets[tabId].comments`). The whole-root snapshot arm copies every root key, so a copied sheet inherits all comment threads and their authors — while `doc` copies drop them (writeDocsRoot never writes `comments`) and `pdf` copies drop them (blob arm attaches no Yorkie doc). docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35 lists comments as an explicit non-goal, so the behaviour is inconsistent across types and contradicts the documented contract.

samples.summary: Copy depends on backend Yorkie attach, which sends no auth token — under `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` the auth webhook denies it, breaking a mainline UI action
samples.evidence: `YorkieService.withDocument` builds `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })` with no `token` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:36-44). `YorkieAuthController.decide` returns UNAUTHENTICATED for a missing/invalid token (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:122-127); it is only fail-open while `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is not `true` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105). Previously this token-less attach was reached only from CLI/v1 REST content endpoints; the new `POST /documents/:id/copy` puts the documents-list 'Make a copy' button on that path, so enabling enforcement would make copying fail for sheet/doc/note/slides/board (and roll back the created row). Confirming needs the deployment's enforce flag value.

finding.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copy re-assigns Yorkie `Long` values as plain JS numbers, re-introducing the 32-bit truncation bug the spreadsheet comment store explicitly works around

verdict.reason: Confirmed as described. `DocumentCopyService.copyContent` takes the JSON_ROOT_TYPES branch for `sheet`/`slides`/`board` (document-copy.service.ts:27,176-198), snapshots the whole root with `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` (snapshotJsonRoot, :209-220) and re-assigns each root key inside `doc.update`, writing every value back as plain JS. Spreadsheet comment threads live in that root (`Worksheet.comments` in packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94, part of SpreadsheetDocument at :115, used by YorkieStore at yorkie-store.ts:69,98), and the frontend store deliberately stores their timestamps as BigInt/Long because Yorkie 0.7.x classifies integer JS numbers as 32-bit Integer (yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14, readers at :16-18 and sheet-view.tsx:246-248; postmortem in docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260512-comments-collab-fixes-lessons.md:3-9 showing truncation to 1970 dates). Nothing in the backend restores bigints (no BigInt/Long usage in packages/backend/src at all) and no code strips comments before the copy, so copied sheets land with Integer-truncated createdAt/editedAt. The cited script precedent (copy-yorkie-documents.ts:316,330 with detachYorkieValue converting bigint→number at :115-118) confirms the same gap rather than guarding it. This is a cross-module invariant violation only visible outside the diff — in lane, major.

finding.summary: Copy depends on backend Yorkie attach, which sends no auth token — under `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` the auth webhook denies it, breaking a mainline UI action
finding.evidence: `YorkieService.withDocument` builds `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })` with no `token` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:36-44). `YorkieAuthController.decide` returns UNAUTHENTICATED for a missing/invalid token (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:122-127); it is only fail-open while `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is not `true` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105). Previously this token-less attach was reached only from CLI/v1 REST content endpoints; the new `POST /documents/:id/copy` puts the documents-list 'Make a copy' button on that path, so enabling enforcement would make copying fail for sheet/doc/note/slides/board (and roll back the created row). Confirming needs the deployment's enforce flag value.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is accurate — YorkieService.withDocument does attach with no token (yorkie.service.ts:36-44) and YorkieAuthController.decide returns 401/UNAUTHENTICATED for a missing token (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:122-127), and the new copy path does use withDocument (document-copy.service.ts:136-198). But the deny is unreachable in this repository's configuration: handleAuth rewrites every non-allowed decision to 200/allowed=true unless `enforce` is set (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:97-105), and `enforce` is only true when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true' (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-88). No config file in the repo sets that variable (grep over yaml/yml/env/json/sh returned nothing); README documents false/shadow as the default (packages/backend/README.md:71-74, 111-113), the design doc makes enforcement an explicitly-gated later ops step (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:196-207), and an in-repo note records enforcement still defaults to false (docs/tasks/active/20260810-notifications-lessons.md:20-22). The webhook must also be registered per-project by an operator, which the repo never does (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:181-194). Additionally, nothing outside the diff is broken: withDocument's contract is unchanged and the identical token-less attach is already used by pre-existing mainline callers (api/v1/cells.controller.ts:53, api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:59, api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:100), so flipping enforcement would break those equally — this is a rollout prerequisite for a disabled flag, not a caller left broken or a guard bypassed by this change.
